summary: Rockstar's open-world crime series, covering the 2D originals, London expansions, 3D-era console and handheld entries, HD-era games, GTA Online, and the announced next entry.

entries.title: Grand Theft Auto

emulation.notes: Use Windows compatibility first; DOSBox is useful for the DOS executable.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original PC assets at clean capture settings

primary.why: The first GTA launched on MS-DOS/Windows and later reached PlayStation and Game Boy Color; Windows is the most practical high-fidelity route for the original 2D game.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release through a modern compatibility wrapper or DOSBox/PCem-style setup if needed; document the exact executable and soundtrack behavior.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern remaster; verify audio and timing behavior on modern systems.

entries.title: Grand Theft Auto: London 1969

emulation.notes: Use Windows compatibility or DOSBox depending on the build.

primary.why: London 1969 is an expansion for the first GTA; Windows keeps the PC fidelity/control route and pairs naturally with the original game.
primary.how_to_play: Install the Windows version alongside the original GTA and document compatibility wrapper or DOSBox settings if used.

entries.remaster_caveats: Requires the original GTA context; no modern remaster.

entries.title: Grand Theft Auto: London 1961

emulation.notes: Use Windows compatibility first, DOSBox if the DOS path is needed.

primary.why: London 1961 was released as a PC mission pack for the original GTA/London setup, making Windows the only meaningful primary route.
primary.how_to_play: Install after the original GTA and London 1969 on Windows; document the exact file set because it depends on the earlier expansion.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern remaster; preserve installer/files with dependency notes.

entries.title: Grand Theft Auto 2

emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original PC assets at clean capture settings

primary.why: Windows is the highest-fidelity and most flexible route for the 2D sequel, ahead of console and handheld ports.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release with modern compatibility fixes; document frame limiter/timing and audio behavior.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern remaster; verify timing/audio on modern systems.

entries.title: Grand Theft Auto III
entries.definitive_edition: Original Windows release with community fixes

emulation.notes: Native Windows route with fixes; PCSX2 optional for PS2 baseline comparison.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original Windows at modern resolution with fix packs

primary.version: Original PC release with community fixes
primary.why: The original Windows release preserves the original art/audio direction while supporting modern resolution and fix packs; the Definitive Edition is higher-level remastering but has documented technical and presentation caveats.
primary.how_to_play: Play the original Windows release with recommended fixes such as widescreen, frame limiter, controller, and SilentPatch-style compatibility fixes; use Definitive Edition only for comparison.

entries.remaster_caveats: The Definitive Edition should be treated as an alternate remaster, not the automatic best version.

entries.definitive_edition: Original Windows release with community fixes

emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original Windows at modern resolution with fix packs

primary.version: Original PC release with community fixes
primary.why: The original Windows release keeps the original presentation and supports modern fixes, while the Definitive Edition has remaster caveats and later releases can be affected by music/licensing changes.

entries.title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas
entries.definitive_edition: Original Windows release with community fixes

emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original Windows at modern resolution with fix packs

primary.version: Original PC release with community fixes
primary.why: The original Windows release is the preferred preservation route because it can be fixed for modern display/control behavior while avoiding the known issues of later mobile-derived/remastered builds.

entries.title: Grand Theft Auto Advance

emulation.notes: Use mGBA for accurate GBA capture.

primary.why: GTA Advance was released only for Game Boy Advance, so a high-accuracy GBA emulator is the best route.
primary.how_to_play: Play with mGBA or original GBA hardware; document emulator, scaling, and save state policy.

entries.remaster_caveats: No remaster; preserve as a handheld entry.

entries.title: Grand Theft Auto: Liberty City Stories

emulation.notes: Use PPSSPP for high internal resolution and stable capture.

primary.why: The PSP original preserves the handheld design and multiplayer-era feature context, and PPSSPP provides the highest-fidelity route without relying on mobile control changes.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PSP version in PPSSPP with high internal resolution; use PS2/mobile only for comparison.

entries.remaster_caveats: Mobile and PS2 ports are alternate routes, not replacements for the PSP original in this archive.

entries.title: Grand Theft Auto: Vice City Stories

emulation.notes: Use PPSSPP for high internal resolution and stable capture.

primary.why: Vice City Stories was designed for PSP and later ported to PS2; PPSSPP gives the highest-fidelity route while preserving the original platform design.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PSP version in PPSSPP with high internal resolution; use PS2 only for comparison.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern remaster or mobile release in the sourced platform list.

entries.title: Grand Theft Auto IV

emulation.notes: Native Windows route; Xbox backward compatibility is useful for comparison.

primary.version: Grand Theft Auto IV: Complete Edition with PC fixes
primary.why: Windows Complete Edition is the highest-fidelity route and bundles the base game with Episodes from Liberty City, but the PC version needs documented fixes for performance and compatibility.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows Complete Edition with recommended fixes/FusionFix-style patches; document patch version, command-line options, and DLC access.

entries.remaster_caveats: No full remaster; Complete Edition changed the PC package and should be documented with patch/build details.

entries.remaster_caveats: Shares GTA IV PC caveats; document build and fixes.

entries.title: Grand Theft Auto: Chinatown Wars

emulation.notes: Use PPSSPP for PSP route; melonDS/DeSmuME only for DS control-context comparison.

primary.why: The PSP version provides higher-resolution presentation than the DS original while preserving the full standalone game; PPSSPP makes it the best fidelity route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PSP version in PPSSPP at high internal resolution; compare DS only if touch-screen mechanics are part of the study.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern remaster; mobile versions are alternate convenience ports.

entries.title: Grand Theft Auto V

primary.why: The 2025 PC Enhanced update brought the newest console-generation features to PC, making Windows the highest-fidelity and most configurable story-mode route.
primary.how_to_play: Play GTAV Enhanced on Windows via Rockstar Launcher, Steam, Epic, Microsoft Store, or PC Game Pass; document Enhanced vs Legacy build, graphics mode, and patch version.

entries.remaster_caveats: Keep Legacy installed only if a specific mod/tool requires it; archive build differences separately.

entries.title: Grand Theft Auto Online

emulation.notes: Native online client only; no offline preservation route for the live service.

primary.why: GTA Online is a live service tied to GTA V; Windows Enhanced/current PC is the most configurable current route, while PS3/Xbox 360 online services are shut down.
primary.how_to_play: Play the current Windows Enhanced GTA Online client; document patch, account/platform, server status, and any current limitations around legacy/modded multiplayer tools.

entries.remaster_caveats: Service-dependent entry; document every archival capture by date and patch.
